nodes.label: Disease Stage
nodes.desc: Clinical stage of advance of the base disease, from mild to terminal.

nodes.label: Depressive Diagnosis (DSM-5)
nodes.desc: DSM-5 depressive disorder category assigned to the patient.

nodes.label: Depressive Episode Type
nodes.desc: Whether the current major depressive episode is a single or recurrent occurrence (DSM-5).

nodes.label: Psychiatric Comorbidities
nodes.desc: Comorbid psychiatric condition present alongside the depressive disorder.

nodes.label: Somatic Symptoms Cluster
nodes.desc: Dominant somatic symptom cluster accompanying the depressive presentation (DSM-5 Criterion A).

nodes.label: Metastatic Disease
nodes.desc: Whether the patient's cancer/disease has metastasized, marking a more advanced disease burden.

nodes.label: Current Chemotherapy
nodes.desc: Whether the patient is currently receiving chemotherapy or other active oncological treatment.

nodes.label: Primary Site: Breast
nodes.desc: Whether breast is the patient's primary cancer site; the most consistently recurring site across the audited advanced-cancer palliative literature.

nodes.label: Primary Site: Lung
nodes.desc: Whether lung is the patient's primary cancer site; consistently among the top 1-2 sites in the audited advanced-cancer palliative cohorts.

nodes.label: Primary Site: Gastrointestinal/Digestive
nodes.desc: Whether the primary cancer site is digestive-tract (colorectal, gastric, esophageal, hepatobiliary, or pancreatic); the single largest pooled site-category across audited cohorts.

nodes.label: Primary Site: Genitourinary/Prostate
nodes.desc: Whether the primary cancer site is genitourinary (prostate, bladder, kidney, or male reproductive organs).

nodes.label: Primary Site: Gynecological
nodes.desc: Whether the primary cancer site is gynecological (ovary, cervix, or uterus, excluding breast).

nodes.label: Primary Site: Hematologic
nodes.desc: Whether the patient's malignancy is hematologic (leukemia, lymphoma) rather than a solid tumor.

nodes.label: Primary Site: Other
nodes.desc: Whether the primary cancer site falls outside the recurring major categories (e.g. head and neck, skin/soft tissue, bone, CNS, sarcoma, unknown primary) — a heterogeneous catch-all, individually low-frequency in the audited cohorts.

nodes.label: Psychoactive Medication
nodes.desc: Current class of psychoactive medication prescribed to the patient, if any.

nodes.label: Opioid Analgesic Use
nodes.desc: Whether the patient is currently on opioid analgesics for pain control.

nodes.label: Antiemetic Use
nodes.desc: Whether the patient is currently on antiemetic medication to control nausea/vomiting.

nodes.label: Opioid-Induced Constipation
nodes.desc: Severity of constipation attributable to opioid analgesic use.

nodes.label: Sedation Level
nodes.desc: Degree of pharmacological sedation from opioids or psychoactive medication.

nodes.label: Nutritional Status (MNA-SF)
nodes.desc: Mini Nutritional Assessment - Short Form score; lower values indicate malnutrition risk.

nodes.label: Functional Autonomy (Barthel ADL)
nodes.desc: Barthel Index of Activities of Daily Living; higher values indicate greater independence.

nodes.label: Instrumental Autonomy (Lawton IADL)
nodes.desc: Lawton-Brody Instrumental Activities of Daily Living score.

nodes.label: Cognitive Function (MMSE)
nodes.desc: Mini-Mental State Examination score; scores below 23/24 suggest cognitive impairment.

nodes.label: Global Performance Status
nodes.desc: Overall functional performance of the patient on a 0-10 scale (protective factor for mood).

nodes.label: ECOG Performance Status
nodes.desc: Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status, 0 (fully active) to 4 (bedridden).

nodes.label: Mobility
nodes.desc: Patient's current level of physical mobility.

nodes.label: Fine Motor Control
nodes.desc: Degree of preserved fine motor control, relevant for app/device usability.

nodes.label: Communication Capacity
nodes.desc: Patient's capacity to communicate verbally.

nodes.label: Chronic Pain
nodes.desc: Chronic pain intensity (ESAS-style 0-10 scale).

nodes.label: Fatigue
nodes.desc: Fatigue intensity (ESAS-style 0-10 scale).

nodes.label: Appetite Loss
nodes.desc: Loss of appetite intensity (ESAS-style 0-10 scale).

nodes.label: Nausea / Vomiting
nodes.desc: Nausea and vomiting intensity (ESAS-style 0-10 scale).

nodes.label: Dyspnea
nodes.desc: Shortness of breath intensity, common in advanced disease.

nodes.label: Drowsiness
nodes.desc: Daytime drowsiness intensity, a common nutrition-impact/medication-related symptom.

nodes.label: Insomnia Severity
nodes.desc: Severity of sleep-onset/maintenance difficulty (DSM-5 Criterion A4).

nodes.label: Depression Severity Index
nodes.desc: Continuous proxy (GDS/HAM-D style, 0-27) for DSM-5 major depressive episode severity specifiers (F32.0-F32.3).

nodes.label: Anxiety Level
nodes.desc: Anxiety symptom intensity, proxy for HADS-A subscale.

nodes.label: Suicidal Ideation Risk
nodes.desc: Latent 0-10 risk score for suicidal ideation (DSM-5 Criterion A9); scores >=7 should trigger the maximum-priority alert protocol.

nodes.label: Spiritual Pain
nodes.desc: Existential/spiritual suffering intensity distinct from physical or mood symptoms.

nodes.label: Distress Level (ESAS)
nodes.desc: General emotional distress, captured by the conversational assistant.

nodes.label: Loneliness (ESAS)
nodes.desc: Sense of loneliness; the system's primary emotional metric.

nodes.label: Death Anxiety (ESAS)
nodes.desc: Fear of death, 0=acceptance to 10=terror; key indicator for Logotherapy vs. CBT selection.

nodes.label: Meaning in Life (ESAS)
nodes.desc: Sense of meaning, 0=existential void to 10=clear sense of meaning; indicator for existential approach.

nodes.label: 7-Day Emotional Trend (ESAS)
nodes.desc: Weighted average of the last 7 emotional check-ins; detects gradual deterioration.

nodes.label: Caregiver Burnout (Zarit)
nodes.desc: Zarit Burden Interview score for the primary caregiver.

nodes.label: Caregiver Type
nodes.desc: Relationship of the primary caregiver to the patient.

nodes.label: Caregiver Contact Frequency
nodes.desc: How often the caregiver is in contact with the patient.

nodes.label: Caregiver-Detected Alert Signals
nodes.desc: Warning signs the caregiver reports observing in day-to-day contact.

nodes.label: Relationship Quality
nodes.desc: Quality of the relationship between patient and caregiver.

nodes.label: Family Support Network
nodes.desc: Size of the patient's family/social support network.

nodes.label: Age Bracket
nodes.desc: Patient age interval; determines the appropriate therapeutic approach by life stage.

nodes.label: Gender
nodes.desc: Patient's gender identity.

nodes.label: Living Environment
nodes.desc: Where the patient currently lives.

nodes.label: Socioeconomic Level
nodes.desc: Socioeconomic stratum, affecting available intervention modality.

nodes.label: Education Level
nodes.desc: Highest education level attained.

nodes.label: Religiosity / Spirituality
nodes.desc: Self-reported degree of religiosity or spirituality; relevant for Logotherapy and existential approaches.

nodes.label: Native Language
nodes.desc: Patient's native/first language; determines the cultural profile of the conversational assistant.

edges.desc: Metastatic disease is associated with worse (higher) ECOG performance status scores.
edges.ref: Article_29 / Article 30 (ECOG-PS worse with metastatic/advanced disease)

edges.desc: Metastatic disease increases baseline chronic pain intensity.
edges.ref: Article_27 (pain present in 79-96% of advanced cancer patients)

edges.desc: Active chemotherapy is one of the nutrition-impact symptoms most strongly associated with higher fatigue burden.
edges.ref: Article_14 (fatigue among strongest NIS associations with depression, p<0.001)

edges.desc: Chronic pain contributes to the overall symptom-burden cluster that includes fatigue.
Opioid analgesics commonly induce daytime drowsiness as a class effect.
edges.ref: Article_14 / Article_27 (drowsiness as a nutrition-impact/opioid-related symptom)

edges.desc: Fatigue and drowsiness co-occur within the same symptom cluster.
Opioid analgesics are a leading pharmacological cause of sedation in palliative patients.
Constipation is the most common and persistent opioid side effect (class effect).
Pain contributes modestly to appetite suppression within the symptom-burden cluster.
Fatigue and appetite loss co-occur as part of the EORTC-style symptom cluster.
edges.ref: Article_28 / Gontijo Garcia et al. 2023 (EORTC symptom cluster, OR 1.12-1.24)

edges.desc: Chemotherapy is a leading cause of treatment-related nausea and vomiting.
edges.ref: Article_14 (nausea among strongest NIS associations with depression, p<0.001)

edges.desc: Lung as primary cancer site directly increases baseline dyspnea/breathlessness burden.
edges.ref: Article_27 (Delgado-Guay et al., lung = largest single site at 37% of sample, dyspnea a core ESAS symptom tracked) / Article_29 (EPCRC, pulmonary diagnosis 17.8%, breathlessness measured as core symptom)

edges.desc: Lung cancer patients show higher depression risk than breast cancer patients in adjusted analysis, used here as the higher-risk reference site.
edges.ref: Article_21 (Atinafu et al., Ethiopia: breast cancer vs. lung cancer adjusted OR 0.1 for depression, p=0.021 — lung as reference category)

edges.desc: Breast cancer diagnosis is associated with markedly lower depression risk relative to lung cancer in adjusted analysis.
edges.ref: Article_21 (Atinafu et al., Ethiopia: breast cancer vs. lung cancer adjusted OR 0.1 for depression, p=0.021)

edges.desc: Gastrointestinal/hepatobiliary/pancreatic primary sites directly increase baseline nausea and vomiting burden.
edges.ref: Article_14 (Amano et al., liver/biliary/pancreas 15.5% + GI tract 14.6% of sample, nausea among strongest NIS associations, p<0.001) / Article_29 (EPCRC, GI 30.4% largest single diagnosis category, nausea measured as core symptom)

edges.desc: Gastrointestinal/hepatobiliary/pancreatic primary sites are the classic drivers of cancer cachexia and appetite loss.
edges.ref: Article_14 (Amano et al., cachexia/refractory cachexia present in 47% of sample dominated by liver/biliary/pancreas/GI sites; lack of appetite p<0.001) / Article_29 (EPCRC, GI 30.4% dominant diagnosis, loss of appetite measured as core symptom, univariate beta -0.32***)

edges.desc: Genitourinary/prostate primary sites (with common bone/pelvic involvement) contribute to chronic pain burden.
edges.ref: Article_27 (Delgado-Guay et al., genitourinary 14% of sample, pain present in 79-96% of the overall advanced-cancer cohort)

edges.desc: Advanced gynecological cancer (ovary/cervix/uterus) directly increases chronic pain burden.
edges.ref: Article_26 (Chan et al., advanced gynecological cancer cohort: pain the most commonly reported physical symptom at 72%, median PPS only 40%)

edges.desc: Advanced gynecological cancer is associated with markedly elevated depression burden relative to the general advanced-cancer population.
edges.ref: Article_26 (Chan et al., HK gynecological cancer cohort: depression prevalence 62%, one of the highest in the audited corpus; stage IV 73.6% of sample)

edges.desc: Hematologic malignancies (leukemia/lymphoma) are classically associated with severe fatigue burden.
edges.ref: Article_25 (Bužgová et al., hematopoiesis 8.0% of advanced-cancer sample) / general oncology-hematology fatigue-burden literature cited across the corpus

edges.desc: Fatigue and nausea co-occur within the EORTC-style symptom cluster.
edges.ref: Article_28 / Gontijo Garcia et al. 2023 (EORTC symptom cluster)

edges.desc: Appetite loss and nausea/vomiting are linked within the EORTC-style symptom cluster.
Antiemetic medication reduces nausea/vomiting intensity.
Worse performance status is associated with greater dyspnea burden in advanced disease.
edges.ref: Article 16 (symptom burden in advanced cancer) / Article_27

edges.desc: Fatigue and insomnia frequently co-occur as depressive somatic symptoms.
Unmanaged pain disrupts sleep onset and maintenance.
edges.ref: Clinical estimate; consistent with DSM-5 somatic symptom criteria

edges.desc: Persistent appetite loss degrades MNA-SF nutritional status score.
edges.ref: Clinical estimate grounded in Article_14 (nutrition impact symptoms)

edges.desc: Nausea and vomiting reduce oral intake and worsen nutritional status.
edges.ref: Article_14 (nutrition impact symptoms and depression association)

edges.desc: Better nutritional status strongly predicts greater functional independence (Barthel ADL).
Better nutritional status predicts greater instrumental autonomy (Lawton IADL).
Better nutritional status is weakly associated with better cognitive function (MMSE).
Better nutritional status strongly predicts lower depression severity.
Greater ADL independence strongly predicts greater IADL independence.
Greater ADL independence is associated with better cognitive function.
Greater ADL independence strongly predicts lower depression severity.
Greater IADL independence is associated with better cognitive function.
Greater IADL independence strongly predicts lower depression severity.
Better cognitive function is weakly associated with lower depression severity.
Worse ECOG performance status reduces overall global performance status.
edges.ref: Article 30 / Article 31 (ECOG-PS as functional outcome measure)

edges.desc: Greater ADL independence modestly contributes to overall global performance.
Higher fatigue reduces overall functional performance.
edges.ref: Article_28 / Gontijo Garcia et al. 2023 (functionality as protective factor, OR .80-.82)

edges.desc: Higher chronic pain reduces overall functional performance.
Higher fatigue is associated with greater depression severity.
Better global performance status is a protective factor against depression severity.
edges.ref: Article_28 / Gontijo Garcia et al. 2023 (OR .80-.82, protective)

edges.desc: Higher spiritual pain erodes the patient's sense of meaning in life.
edges.ref: Article 39 / Pérez-Cruz et al. 2019 (spiritual pain decreases quality of life)

edges.desc: Spiritual/existential suffering contributes to overall emotional distress.
Chronic pain intensity is moderately correlated with emotional distress/anxiety.
edges.ref: Article_27 (HADS-A x ESAS symptom correlations, r=0.25-0.5)

edges.desc: Higher depression severity is associated with greater day-to-day distress.
edges.ref: js/schema.js clinical estimate, moderated for system consistency

edges.desc: Higher general distress is associated with greater fear of death.
Spiritual/existential suffering amplifies fear of death.
Higher distress is associated with lower sense of meaning (existential void).
General distress is strongly correlated with anxiety symptom intensity.
edges.ref: Article_27 (HADS-A x ESAS-Anxiety item, r=0.56, p<0.001)

edges.desc: Pain intensity is moderately correlated with anxiety.
edges.ref: Article_27 (HADS-A x ESAS symptom correlations, r=0.25-0.5)

edges.desc: Nausea/vomiting is one of the symptoms most distinctly elevated in anxious patients.
Dyspnea is moderately correlated with anxiety symptom intensity.
edges.ref: Article_27 (HADS-A x ESAS symptom correlations, r=0.25-0.5)

edges.desc: Higher distress is associated with greater sense of loneliness.
Greater sense of meaning is associated with lower loneliness.
Distress level strongly informs the 7-day weighted emotional trend (same scale/window).
Sustained loneliness contributes to the 7-day emotional trend.
Higher patient loneliness is associated with greater caregiver burden.
Depression severity is the strongest driver of suicidal ideation risk.
edges.ref: DSM-5 Criterion A9 (recurrent thoughts of death/suicidal ideation) / Article 32 (self-harm thoughts strongly associated with higher PHQ-9 scores)

edges.desc: Acute emotional distress amplifies suicidal ideation risk.
edges.ref: Clinical estimate consistent with DSM-5 risk factors

edges.desc: Social isolation/loneliness is a recognized risk factor for suicidal ideation.
edges.ref: Article 15 (family cohesion protective against anxiety/depression) / clinical risk-factor literature

edges.desc: A stronger sense of meaning is protective against suicidal ideation.
Lower socioeconomic stratum is associated with worse nutritional status.
edges.ref: Efendioglu et al. 2021 (OR=.10 for malnutrition in low-income patients)

edges.desc: Lower socioeconomic stratum is associated with higher depression severity.
edges.ref: Efendioglu et al. 2021 (OR=.06 for depression in low-income patients)

edges.desc: Advanced age (71+) is associated with worse nutritional status.
Advanced age (71+) is associated with higher depression severity.
Terminal-stage disease is associated with markedly lower global performance status.
edges.ref: Article_28 / Gontijo Garcia et al. 2023 (functionality as protective factor)

edges.desc: Terminal-stage disease is associated with higher symptomatic fatigue burden.
edges.ref: Article_28 / Gontijo Garcia et al. 2023 (advanced-stage symptom burden)

edges.desc: Terminal-stage disease is associated with greater appetite loss.
edges.ref: Article_28 / Gontijo Garcia et al. 2023 (advanced-stage symptom burden)

edges.desc: Terminal-stage disease is associated with greater nausea/vomiting burden.
edges.ref: Article_28 / Gontijo Garcia et al. 2023 (advanced-stage symptom burden)

edges.desc: Absence of a family support network is associated with greater loneliness.
Absence of a family support network is associated with higher depression severity.
Being bedridden is associated with markedly lower global performance status.
Being bedridden is definitionally associated with lower Barthel ADL scores.
A conflictive caregiver relationship is associated with greater patient loneliness.
Loss of verbal communication capacity is associated with greater loneliness.
Caregiver-reported alert signals (crying, isolation, refusal to eat) proxy for higher depression severity.
edges.ref: Clinical estimate; ACOMPANAR_Algoritmo_v1.pdf (caregiver as primary sensor)

edges.desc: A comorbid anxiety disorder diagnosis correlates with higher measured anxiety level.
edges.ref: DSM-5 (depressive disorder 'with anxiety' specifier) / clinical estimate

edges.desc: Insomnia as the dominant somatic symptom cluster directly correlates with insomnia severity.
edges.ref: DSM-5 Criterion A4 (insomnia or hypersomnia nearly every day)

edges.desc: Severe fatigue as the dominant somatic symptom cluster correlates with measured fatigue.
edges.ref: DSM-5 Criterion A6 (fatigue or loss of energy nearly every day)

edges.desc: Sedating psychoactive medications (antidepressants, anxiolytics, antipsychotics) correlate with higher sedation.
A major depressive disorder diagnosis correlates strongly with a higher depression severity index.
Higher religiosity/spirituality is associated with a stronger sense of meaning in life.
Direct family caregivers tend to report higher burnout than professional caregivers.
24/7 in-home caregiving contact is associated with higher caregiver burnout.
Living alone is associated with greater patient loneliness.
Metastatic disease burden is associated with higher depression severity.
edges.ref: Article_29 / Article 30 (metastatic disease and worse QoL/depression outcomes)
